hint.text:
Question tags such as “is he?” or “didn’t you?” should not be used in formal speech and writing. Questions can still be used in formal speech and writing, but they should be written formally.

Informal: You'll come to the shops with me, right?

Formal: Will you come to the shops with me?
hint.sound: Question tags such as “Is he?” or “didn’t you?” should not be used in formal speech and writing. Questions can still be used in formal speech and writing, but they should be written formally. For example, informally you could say 'You'll come to the shops with me, right?' and formally you could say 'Will you come to the shops with me?'

instruction.text: Select a formal question to replace the informal question.

b: You didn’t hurt yourself, did you?
Wait, have you already hurt yourself?

atoms.a: You won’t tell anyone, will you?
The cake has already been delivered, hasn’t it?
b: The cake was delivered, weren’t it?

instruction.text: Choose the formal question to add at the end of the sentence.

atoms.a: It is awful that we cut down so many trees.
b: It’s crazy how people are ok with it, right?
++Do they not think about the environmental effects?
What about the environmental effects, you know?

atoms.a: We must discuss the increasing rate of climate change.
b: ++What can we do to slow it down?
I mean we have to slow it down, right?
